ev.q: Of 343 company employees who completed a questionnaire and ate luncheon food, 191 (56%) had an illness meeting the case definition.
Of 236 luncheon attendees who ate potato salad, 183 (78%) became ill.
Illness onsets occurred a median of 33 hours after eating the lunch (range: 6--96 hours)
the median duration of illness was 24 hours (range: 5--120 hours)
Nineteen (53%) of the residents had illnesses meeting the case definition.
Among luncheon attendees, eating potato salad was associated strongly with illness (odds ratio=42.7; 95% confidence interval=18.6--101.7).

public_health_question.v: What were the sources and modes of transmission of two Norwalk-like virus gastroenteritis outbreaks (foodborne in Alaska, person-to-person in Wisconsin)?

ev.q: This report presents investigations of a foodborne NLV outbreak in Alaska and person-to-person transmission in Wisconsin.
Outbreaks of Norwalk-like Viral Gastroenteritis --- Alaska and Wisconsin, 1999
This report presents investigations of a foodborne NLV outbreak in Alaska and person-to-person transmission in Wisconsin.
On November 11, questionnaires were e-mailed to 500 company employees; 456 (91%) were returned.
All residents of the involved floor were administered a symptom, event, and food history questionnaire.

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension is reported; populations are defined by employer and residence hall, and no age, sex or other SPD results are given.

notes: The Wisconsin statement that no event, meal, food or beverage 'was associated with illness' implies an unstated comparison; no test or measure is reported, so no procedure is recorded. RT-PCR and sequencing only confirm cases and link them, so they are not procedures. The 51-outbreak transmission percentages are cited from an earlier study.
